item.title: Yella Beezy Defense Challenges $40,000 Payment Theory In MO3 Trial
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Yella Beezy's defense pressed the lead detective on cash evidence and witness accounts as the MO3 murder trial's second week ended.
item.content:encoded:
Yella Beezy‘s defense challenged the money trail and witness accounts at the center of his MO3 murder case Friday, pressing the lead detective on what police could prove about a $40,000 cash withdrawal.

Dallas Police Detective Eric Barnes faced cross-examination from attorney Toby Shook as the trial’s second week ended November 6.

The defense questioned whether investigators could connect the rapper’s cash to the killing and whether phone records supported a key witness’s account.

Yella Beezy, whose legal name is Markies Conway, has pleaded not guilty to capital murder and denied involvement.

Prosecutors accuse him of paying Kewon White to kill MO3, born Melvin Noble, on Interstate 35 in November 2020.

White was convicted of capital murder in September and sentenced to life in prison.

Shook walked Barnes through Yella Beezy’s Chase Bank records and challenged the state’s claim that a $40,000 withdrawal funded the alleged hit.

The November 20, 2020, transaction occurred nine days after MO3’s killing, not before it.

The defense pointed to other large withdrawals following a $350,000 record-label wire transfer.

Barnes acknowledged he did not know how Yella Beezy spent the money. Shook argued that carrying cash and making luxury purchases fit the rapper’s usual spending.

Shook also showed an Instagram video dated November 23, 2020, in which Yella Beezy dealt out $100 bills on a table.

The defense argued the footage undercut the claim that he had handed over the withdrawn funds. The video itself did not establish the source of each bill.

The denominations became another point of dispute.

Shook questioned Barnes about footage showing White with bundles of smaller bills at an Arlington jewelry store before an alleged meeting tied to Yella Beezy.

The bank withdrawal consisted of $100 and $50 bills. Barnes acknowledged that investigators could not trace the recovered cash directly to Yella Beezy’s bank withdrawal.

Shook then challenged testimony about an alleged confession at a South Dallas barbershop. He cited FBI cell-tower analysis placing Yella Beezy’s phone roughly 40 miles north in Frisco at the relevant time. Barnes acknowledged police had no corroborating evidence placing the rapper at the barbershop.

The defense also returned to Theodore Thomas’s credibility.

Thomas had denied Yella Beezy’s involvement in an earlier interview and later recanted his grand jury account. Shook questioned Barnes about the witness’s changing story and the federal charges Thomas faced before cooperating.

Earlier in Friday’s testimony, prosecutors and the defense offered different readings of a message attributed to Yella Beezy.

Prosecutors argued it showed he had people who “will do the shootings” for him. The defense argued the message referred to security, not hired killers.

One redacted message stated: “We all told him, don’t grab no gun. We got other [men] for that.”

Judge Chika Anyiam allowed the disputed message into evidence. The judge also barred jurors from hearing White’s recorded jail remarks about payment while allowing references to bail discussions.

The cross-examination followed Thursday’s presentation of music videos, social media posts and a 2019 interview. Prosecutors used that material to outline the feud they say supplied a motive for MO3’s killing.

They also presented footage of an assault on MO3’s manager, Brandon Rainwater, and discussed the song “Keep It in the Streets.”

Shook offered an alternative theory involving co-defendant Devin Brown, who is separately charged with capital murder.

The defense pointed to Brown’s conflict with MO3 over the mother of Brown’s children and videos showing Brown with cash.

Shook argued that Brown had his own motive and access to money. Those arguments remain part of the defense’s challenge to the prosecution’s case, not findings by the jury.

Yella Beezy faces life in prison if convicted. The jury has not reached a verdict.

item.title: Kanye West Breaks U.S. Rap Attendance Record With 83,000-Ticket Dallas Show
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Kanye West's AT&T Stadium show sold 83,000 tickets and earned $16.5 million, IKON told The Breakfast Club's Loren Lorosa.
item.content:encoded:
Kanye West broke another rap attendance record at AT&T Stadium, where the venue declared his November 7 concert the most-attended rap show in U.S. history and promoter IKON Presents reported 83,000 tickets sold.

The Dallas-area stop generated $18 million in revenue, according to figures an IKON representative supplied to Loren Lorosa of The Breakfast Club.

Lorosa reported the numbers after Ye’s stadium show in Arlington, Texas, marking a new high for the independent run just one week after Houston.

“YE LIVE! In Dallas at AT&T Stadium sold 83,000 tickets and generated $16.5 million in revenue, exceeding the promoter’s reported 74,412 tickets sold at last week’s Houston show,” Lorosa wrote, citing the company producing the stadium run.

She closed the update with another point from the promoter: “100% independent tour.”

AT&T Stadium celebrated the result in its own post Sunday morning, writing “history made” before announcing that “@kanyewest headlines the most attended rap show in US history at AT&T Stadium.”

The Dallas ticket total was 8,588 higher than the Houston sales figure IKON gave Lorosa. That Houston concert took place on Halloween at Reliant Stadium, making the two Texas dates back-to-back milestones for the same run.

Ye had already put up large numbers in several other markets this year. His April shows at SoFi Stadium in the Los Angeles area sold a combined 140,480 tickets and grossed $33 million.

His Chicago homecoming at Soldier Field drew approximately 142,000 fans across September 3 and 4, with roughly 71,000 people attending each night. Those figures covered two shows, while IKON’s new Dallas total covered one.

The run also drew more than 65,000 people to the Caesars Superdome in New Orleans in August and more than 60,000 to San Antonio’s Alamodome on July 4.

IKON had stressed the scale of the operation before the latest Texas concerts. In an October statement promoting its record-setting stadium demand, the company described YE Live as operating through “an independent touring structure outside the traditional major-promoter model.”

The company said that structure covered venue coordination, ticketing, production, security, staffing and transportation while giving artists and their partners a greater role in building the shows. Organizers also said the broader live run had passed one million fans worldwide.

Ye’s announced U.S. stadium dates continue November 21 at State Farm Stadium in the Phoenix area. He has also booked Mexico City’s Estadio Banorte for March 19, 2027.

item.title: Dame Dash Says Jermaine Dupri Blocked His Janet Jackson Pursuit
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Dame Dash recalled asking Jermaine Dupri for Janet Jackson's phone number and claimed the producer still held it against him.
item.content:encoded:
Dame Dash said he once asked Jermaine Dupri for Janet Jackson’s phone number, even though Dupri was dating her, and claimed the producer still held it against him.

The Roc-A-Fella Records co-founder shared his version of the exchange in an interview with The Art of Dialogue.

Asked whether he had ever tried to pursue Jackson, Dash gave a blunt answer.

“Of course. I try to get everybody,” he said. “Jermaine was hating. You still mad about that stuff up there.”

Dash said he had obtained Jackson’s number before and wanted it again. But by that point, he said, Dupri was with her. Dash recalled seeing the producer around Jackson while doubting that the two were a couple.

In Dash’s telling, Jackson directed him to Dupri when he asked for her number. Dash said he then went to Dupri and asked him to pass it along. The request did not get him what he wanted.

“He was like chill chill,” Dash recalled. “I was like you’re not messing with her anyway. Give me the number but he wouldn’t give me the number.”

Dash framed the story as an example of how he approached dating when he was younger. He described himself as a man in his twenties who felt confident about his place in the music business and his appeal to women.

“I’m trying to get at everything. Just bottom line in the most respectful way. I was doing my big one,” he said.

Jackson and Dupri’s relationship became one of music’s best-known pairings in the 2000s.

They split in 2009 after years together. Their history also included work in the studio, with Dupri contributing to Jackson’s music.

For Dash, the story centered on his refusal to believe Dupri was dating Jackson. He defended his actions by pointing to how young he was.

“I was young. You know that’s what you’re supposed to do if you’re a heterosexual man and you’re the coolest in the world and all the women like you. What I’m supposed to do?” Dash said.

item.title: Dana White Sets Trump Meeting Over White House Press Secretary Offer
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Dana White will meet Donald Trump on Monday after the president offered the UFC boss the vacant White House press secretary role.
item.content:encoded:
Dana White is headed for a Monday meeting with President Donald Trump after the president offered him the vacant White House press secretary job.

White confirmed the meeting while speaking to reporters at a boxing event in London. The UFC chief said he planned to fly straight to Washington and expected the conversation to bring more clarity to an offer that immediately blurred politics, sports and spectacle.

Trump announced the offer in a social media post Saturday. He described White as a fighter and said the longtime combat-sports executive could bring UFC figures with him as assistants. White then shared the president’s message and an image of himself behind the White House briefing-room podium.

“I am pleased to announce that the Great Dana White, a violent Fighter and Warrior, has been offered the job of Press Secretary of the United States,” Donald Trump wrote on Truth Social. “I have requested that he bring with him assistants, even though some are not from our Country, of Islam Makhachev, Khabib Nurmagomedov, Justin Gaethje, Daniel Cormier, Amanda Nunes, and Kayla Harris. We need these people to defend us against the Lunatic Left. Dana will be a Press Secretary like none other. Dana, please take the job!”

The public response stopped short of an acceptance. Asked how he could add a government role to his existing workload, White said, “Yeah, I got a lot of jobs already.”

The press secretary speaks for the president and handles regular briefings with reporters. The role demands quick answers on policy, personnel and events that can shift by the hour. White has spent years running news conferences, but the White House job carries a different level of public scrutiny.

White runs UFC and has also been building Zuffa Boxing with Saudi backing. His next steps in Washington could pull one of combat sports’ most recognizable executives into a daily role speaking for the president and answering questions from the White House press corps.

The offer arrived during a wider reset inside the administration. Trump named Stephen Miller to replace Susie Wiles as chief of staff after Republicans lost control of both chambers of Congress in the midterm elections. Katie Zacharia left the press secretary post after five days, and the job had already been open since Karoline Leavitt departed in August.

White and Trump have maintained a close relationship for years. White spoke at the Republican National Conventions in 2016, 2020 and 2024. Trump has appeared at UFC events, while White helped bring a UFC show to the White House lawn during the nation’s 250th anniversary celebration in June.

White declined to describe his earlier talks with Trump. “I’m sure I’ll have more to talk about after that,” he said of Monday’s meeting.

item.title: Adrien Broner Reportedly Taken To Hospital After Night Out With Blueface
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Adrien Broner reportedly needed emergency help at a concert with Blueface before being taken to a hospital, according to KickChamp.
item.content:encoded:
Adrien Broner was reportedly taken to a hospital after needing emergency help during a concert outing with Blueface.

The former boxing champion’s medical scare unfolded on a Kick livestream.

Blueface and members of his team helped carry Broner down a flight of stairs when he could no longer manage on his own. Emergency workers attended to him as people nearby grew concerned that he was becoming unresponsive.

The group remained around Broner while medics tried to get him seated. He was eventually placed in a wheelchair and taken out of the venue for further treatment, according to the report, which said he was then transported to a hospital.

The report did not include a medical diagnosis or an update on his condition after the hospital trip.

The 37-year-old Cincinnati native has spent much of his time away from boxing in front of livestream cameras, regularly appearing with DeenTheGreat. Their partnership recently moved into music through a joint release with Hitmaka.

The pair put out “Purple App Killa,” a diss track aimed at Kai Cenat, on October 15 after sharing behind-the-scenes footage of work on the song and video.

The release followed DeenTheGreat’s public complaint about a visit to Cenat’s Vivet clothing stand at ComplexCon, where he said he felt he had been treated like a random fan.

Boxing remained part of Broner’s plans even as those online appearances filled his schedule. Over the summer, he returned to training and began cutting off his streams at 10 p.m. as he worked toward another comeback.

Before his streaming career, Broner won world titles at junior lightweight, lightweight, welterweight and junior welterweight.

He captured his third divisional championship by beating Paulie Malignaggi in 2013, then added the fourth with a stoppage of Khabib Allakhverdiev in his hometown in 2015. He was 26 when he completed that run, which spanned divisions from 130 to 147 pounds.

His last professional fight came in June 2024 against Blair Cobbs in Hollywood, Florida. Cobbs knocked him down in the second round and won a unanimous decision over 10 rounds, leaving Broner with a record of 35 wins, five losses and one draw.

item.title: Druski Makes SNL History With Whiteface Sketch
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Druski made SNL history as its first digital creator host, mixing an Emma Stone cameo with a wild Elizabeth Holmes sketch.
item.content:encoded:
Druski made “Saturday Night Live” history with a debut that turned his online comedy instincts into a full network showcase.

The Georgia-born creator became the first personality known primarily for digital content to host the long-running NBC show.

The Strokes served as musical guests, but the night belonged to a comedian who built his audience through short sketches, recurring characters and the mock music business of Coulda Been Records.

His monologue leaned into that jump from the internet to live television. Emma Stone walked onstage during a bit about a movie called “The Catch,” playing along as Druski described himself as her new co-star.

He also joked about the limits producers placed on his comedy and said he could not promise “no whiteface.”

That line paid off later in “Dru Can See Everything,” a sketch built around disgraced Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes. Jane Wickline played Holmes, while Ben Marshall played her husband, Billy Evans. Their characters visited Druski for a psychic reading as Holmes prepared to report to prison.

Druski played himself, but the sketch gave him room to change voices and appearances as he claimed to see pieces of Holmes’ future. The most pointed visual sent him into Holmes’ black turtleneck, blond hair and deep voice, turning his earlier warning into the night’s most direct callback.

The episode also let him move beyond one viral character. He worked through political material, family jokes and ensemble sketches with the cast, a broader test than the tightly edited videos that made him famous.

The booking arrived days after Druski announced a multiyear Netflix agreement. AllHipHop previously reported that the deal covers new projects and licenses several shows he financed and developed for his own audience. His scripted comedy “Collect & Praise,” with Mike Epps, is due in December.

That timing made the SNL appearance more than a celebrity victory lap. It put the creator in front of a television audience just as his self-built operation moves into a larger production deal.

Druski ended the night with the same approach that built his career: committing to the character, pushing the joke until it became uncomfortable and letting the audience decide where the line sat.

item.title: Lil Uzi Vert Takes Over Fortnite For 24-Hour Captain’s Day
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Lil Uzi Vert becomes Fortnite's Captain's Day boss for 24 hours with a new weapon, Sprite and boosted event drops.
item.content:encoded:
Lil Uzi Vert is taking command of Fortnite’s Stronghold for a 24-hour Captain’s Day event built around a boss fight, a custom weapon and a pint-sized Sprite.

Epic Games announced that the Philadelphia rapper becomes this week’s boss on Sunday (November 8). The event begins at 9 A.M. ET and runs for one day, giving players a limited window to challenge Uzi and claim the new loot.

“A new captain sails in with new loot!” Epic said in its event notice.

Defeating the boss can unlock Lil Uzi Vert’s Lil’ SMG, which fires faster the longer a player holds the trigger. The weapon also adds a movement-speed boost, giving the reward a practical use beyond the celebrity crossover.

The takeover also introduces the Lil Uzi Vert Jr. Sprite. Restoring shields with the character triggers a Chug Splash effect, while special Sprite variants will drop more often during the event.

Cursed Sprites begin appearing in the wild at the same time, and a second Map Fragment joins the season’s treasure hunt.

Fortnite has been rolling out its Treasure Hunters season through a rotating lineup of captains. The Straw Hats and A$AP Rocky led the opening week before Uzi’s arrival. Cap’n Hatsune Miku and Kasane Teto are also scheduled to enter the rotation as the season moves forward.

The season is set on an 80-player Crossbones Isle filled with One Piece locations and powers. Captain’s Days add new weapons and Sprites on selected dates, while other recurring events change drop rates and rewards.

That setup makes Uzi’s appearance part of the season’s weekly progression, not a permanent map change.

Uzi’s Captain’s Day role is separate from the rapper’s Item Shop arrival. Epic has listed the Lil Uzi Vert shop release for November 12, four days after the Stronghold takeover begins. The company has not announced a price for the cosmetic release.

The crossover puts Uzi inside one of gaming’s biggest live worlds at a moment when Fortnite is leaning heavily into music, anime and celebrity characters.

For players, the immediate stakes are simple: find the boss, win the fight and collect the limited-time weapon and Sprite before the 24-hour window closes.

item.title: Imposter Claiming To Be Sexyy Red’s Manager Arrested In New Rape Case
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: A man accused of posing as Sexyy Red's manager faces new sexual battery and false imprisonment charges in South Florida.
item.content:encoded:
A South Florida man accused of posing as Sexyy Red’s manager is back in custody after Hialeah police charged him in a new sexual battery case.

Vladimir Jean-Joseph, 43, faces sexual battery and false imprisonment charges tied to an alleged Halloween weekend attack.

Local 10 News reported that the accuser, an Orlando woman, told detectives she met Jean-Joseph at a club in May. She said he introduced himself as “the manager for rapper Sexyy Red.”

Police said the two stayed in touch. According to the arrest report, Jean-Joseph later offered the woman and her friends a free place to stay while they visited South Florida. The woman returned alone to the Hialeah apartment after a night out in Miami Beach and went to sleep.

Investigators said Jean-Joseph entered her bedroom without permission, got into bed and began touching her. The woman told police she rejected his advances, but he allegedly sexually assaulted her and tried to force her to perform oral sex.

A friend took the woman to HCA Florida JFK Hospital, where medical staff completed a sexual assault examination. Detectives arrested Jean-Joseph on Lincoln Road in Miami Beach days later.

The accusation follows a separate 2024 case involving the same alleged false claim about the St. Louis rapper. In that case, a woman told Miami Gardens police that Jean-Joseph approached her after a Sexyy Red event, called himself “Alexander Beamer,” and claimed to represent the artist.

Sexyy Red’s spokesperson was direct at the time: “Vladimir Joseph is not her manager.”

AllHipHop reported in 2024 that police accused Jean-Joseph of taking the woman to his home, threatening her with a gun, forcing her to ingest cocaine and sexually assaulting her.

Prosecutors dropped those charges two months later. The reason was not immediately available, and the station said it requested records explaining the decision.

The current charges pertain to one woman. A second woman also alleged an assault, according to the new arrest report, but police said she had not met with detectives to give a statement.

Jean-Joseph was already free on bond in a separate case involving allegations of resisting arrest and battery on a law enforcement officer. Jail records cited by Local 10 showed him held at the Metrowest Detention Center after the latest arrest.

item.title: Michael Che Says He Didn’t Know Kanye West Video Was Being Filmed
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Michael Che says he didn't know his Kanye West confrontation was filmed and recalls Dave Chappelle's effort to end their feud.
item.content:encoded:
Michael Che opened up about the viral leaked video of him confronting Kanye West during an appearance on “What Now? with Trevor Noah.” The SNL writer and cast member revealed he had no idea he was being filmed when the backstage moment occurred, and only found out about the video when it suddenly appeared on social media feeds years later.

“I don’t know who taped that. I don’t know where that came from. I never talked about it. Nobody ever mentioned it. And then all of a sudden it’s just everywhere,” Che explained. “I would never said any of that stuff on a camera. I didn’t I didn’t know that.” The video resurfaced unexpectedly, catching both Che and host Trevor Noah off guard when it appeared in their YouTube recommendations.

During the interview, Che walked through the intense process of hosting Saturday Night Live, describing it as a grueling week that starts Monday with meetings and pitches, builds through a seven-to-eight-hour table read of about 40 sketches on Wednesday, and culminates in pre-tapes that can run until 4 A.M. on Friday before the live show on Saturday. “It feels like we’re planning someone else’s wedding every time,” Che said, explaining the high stakes and stress involved.

Regarding the Kanye situation, Che expressed frustration about the lack of consent when the video was filmed. “If you’re taping people at work, you should get some kind of consent form, right?” he said. The tension between Che and West eventually eased thanks to an unexpected intervention from Dave Chappelle. After a mass shooting in Dayton, Ohio, Chappelle was organizing a charity show and decided to reconcile the two. “He was like, ‘I’m picking up Kanye from the airport. I want you to come with me to pick him up. We’re going to bury the hatchet with this Kanye thing,'” Che recalled. Despite his initial resistance, Che agreed to the meeting, showing how even the most contentious celebrity conflicts can find resolution through mutual friends and shared humanity.

item.title: Meta, Google And TikTok Sue California Over Teen Feed Limits
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Meta, Google and TikTok want a federal court to block California's new limits on autoplay and personalized feeds for minors.
item.content:encoded:
Meta, Google and TikTok have filed separate federal lawsuits seeking to block a California law that would restrict autoplay, personalized recommendations and other features for users younger than 16.

The companies sued California Attorney General Rob Bonta on November 4, arguing Assembly Bill 1709 violates the First Amendment and conflicts with Section 230 of the Communications Decency Act. The law is scheduled to take effect on January 1, 2027.

Meta and Google filed in the Northern District of California, while TikTok brought its challenge in the Central District. Each complaint seeks declaratory and injunctive relief before the new restrictions take effect.

Governor Gavin Newsom signed AB 1709 in September as part of a broader child-safety package. It bars covered platforms from giving children under 16 access to features the state defines as addictive, including autoplay and algorithmic feeds built from a user’s history and profile. Platforms also must use age-assurance measures.

Meta said the measure tries to “appoint the State as the editor, curator and controller of online speech.” Its complaint argues California cannot override the company’s editorial judgment about how Facebook, Instagram and Threads organize posts.

TikTok called the law “a blatantly unconstitutional restriction on free expression.” The company also argued that California would take a decision away from parents who use its Family Pairing tools, daily limits and Restricted Mode but still allow a teenager to receive a personalized feed.

Google said broad restrictions could disrupt systems designed to steer younger users toward age-appropriate videos. Spokesman Jose Castaneda said, “Overly broad laws like this actually break the systems we’ve built to help kids find high-quality, age-appropriate videos.”

The challenge arrives amid growing legal pressure over youth social-media use. Meta agreed in August to pay as much as $18 billion and strengthen child-safety controls to settle claims tied to teen addiction. TikTok separately settled an Alabama case over allegedly addictive features in September.

California is already defending Senate Bill 976, an earlier law limiting addictive feeds for minors unless a platform obtains parental consent. That case is expected to reach the Ninth Circuit next spring, while AB 1709 removes the parental-consent option for the features covered by the newer law.

The companies are asking courts in Northern and Central California to stop AB 1709 before its effective date. Bonta’s office said it was reviewing the complaints and remained committed to defending California’s online protections for children.
